findings.finding: checks.cjs now exports { checks, rangeChecks }. Its two importers, verify.cjs and verification.test.js, moved in the same commit. Each snapshot runs its own verify.cjs, so older commits keep their own shape. The UI branches do not edit these files, so they rebase without conflict.
After this merges, every branch that rebases onto main needs a skill record before verify:commit or the pre-push hook passes.
findings.none: Reported to the owner as a rollout decision.

findings.finding: CI checks out one commit without history, so verify:current cannot find a merge base.
findings.none: verify:current skips range checks without --base and prints that it did; the workflow change is a separate patch because the bot cannot push workflows.

findings.finding: Requiring a patch on every citation fails every existing record until skills:record refills it. Records 1 and 2 were refilled on this branch.
findings.none: Later branches refill theirs in their own record commits.

findings.finding: verify:push now fails a pushed branch with no commits ahead of origin/main. The CI patch's push to main runs verify:current, which reports an empty range as not run and still exits 0.
findings.none: Documented in docs/skills.md and the CI note.

findings.finding: Second author pass: a later change that edits an earlier change's record pulls that record into its own range. On work/skill-process-2b, skills:check from the PR1 head fails on record 1's citations and its boundary-discipline entry, because 467868b refilled record 1's patch-ids inside PR2. From origin/main it passes. docs/skills.md said stacked branches do not conflict.
An earlier draft of writeRecord deleted records already merged at the base, which added a deletion to every later change.
findings.none: Removed before the first commit; records stay, as docs/skills.md explains.

findings.finding: citePatch catches a failed rev-parse. A record can cite a SHA that does not exist, and the check must then report it, so the catch is at a boundary.
Three comments remain: the range-check argument contract in checks.cjs, why verify.cjs resolves the base in the source repository, and why the fixture base holds a merged record.
findings.none: Each states a constraint the code cannot show.

findings.finding: Second author pass, audited inline because this pass runs without subagents: the patchIds comment overstated when a copy keeps its patch-id, so it now names the conflict case. The range-check argument contract in checks.cjs and the base-ref note in verify.cjs describe contracts the code cannot show.

Found in independent review: citations failed after every cherry-pick, because the check matched findings to commits only by SHA. Citations now carry the commit's patch-id, which a cherry-pick keeps. Before the fix, the cherry-picked work/skill-process-2b failed with four citations outside the range.

Found in independent review: verify:current printed a plain PASS without --base, and verify:commit --base HEAD passed range checks over zero commits. Both came from deciding on the presence of a base instead of the size of the range.
The default export of checks.cjs became a named pair.
findings.none: Both callers moved in the same commit, and nothing else imports it on any local branch.

findings.finding: records.cjs is a new file next to routing.cjs.
findings.none: The record format and check are a separate concern from routing; merging them would make routing.cjs 450 lines.

findings.finding: Eight mutations each failed a test: coverage off, any commit counts, unknown skill allowed, unresolved finding allowed, deleted record read, unchanged records counted, duplicates allowed, and no range checks in verify:commit.
The first commit attempt of 685401e failed because the shell PATH lacked Node 22.23.3; the hook reported Use Node 22.23.3.
findings.none: Environment, not code; the retry used the pinned Node.

findings.finding: Commits between the verify wiring and the record fail the range check by design.
findings.none: The pre-push hook and verify:commit check branch tips, and the tip carries the record.

findings.finding: The resolution transform needed an inverse serialize step to write records back.

The first mutation for unchanged records only removed the deleted-file filter, which no test covered; the clean case now deletes the merged record and a separate mutation reads every record in the tree.
The committed-and-staged test pinned the range checks running with the commit as its own base, so it asserted the empty-range defect. Its fixture now has an earlier main.

Nine mutations of the citation and range logic fail the tests: SHA-only matching, an optional patch, a mismatched patch, no SHA rewrite, no patch fill, an allowed empty commit range, range checks over an empty current range, no notRun field, and a plain PASS.
docs/skills.md lists each failure the check reports and states what a pass does not prove.
AGENTS.md and README.md said each finding was resolved. The check proves only that each finding has a resolution.

Second author pass: docs/skills.md and the patchIds comment said every cherry-picked or rebased copy keeps its patch-id. Building work/skill-process-2c, the copy of 467868b conflicted in record 1 and its patch-id changed, while the eight clean copies kept theirs.
The verify test asserts the recorded command and base in result.json rather than the check output.
findings.none: The recorded command is the contract between verify and the checks.

findings.finding: Parsed records had a different shape from stored records, so every write had to translate back.
The change-id pattern was repeated in the CLI and the records module.
The range decision added three conditions to verify, which crossed the complexity limit of 20.
findings.none: Moved into planRanges before the commit, which keeps verify as orchestration.

findings.finding: Checked the new AGENTS.md, README.md, and docs/skills.md text for filler, long dashes, and mid-sentence colons.
The AGENTS.md line names the trigger (before you push), the command, and the limit of the check.
The AGENTS.md record line claimed more than the check proves.
